newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas planting progressed despite cool weather.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas planting progressed despite cool weather.

text.p: Planting of corn, cotton, rice, sorghum and soybeans was under way in the week ended Sunday despite below normal temperatures and scattered showers, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.

Soybean were 14 percent planted and three percent emerged versus nine and none, respectively, a year ago and six and one for the averages. The crop was rated 24 percent good, 65 fair, none poor and 11 very poor.
Corn was 97 percent planted the same as a year ago and the 90 average. The crop was rated one percent excellent, 41 good, 53 fair, four poor and one very poor.
Rice was 60 percent planted and 21 emerged versus 56 and 28, respectively, a year ago and the 61 and 35 averages. The crop was rated five percent excellent, 39 good, 46 fair, and ten poor.
Cotton was seven percent planted versus 19 a year ago and the 26 average.
Sorghum was 57 percent planted and 29 emerged versus 53 and 31, respectively, a year ago and 52 and 33 for the averages.
Winter wheat was 90 percent headed versus 57 a year ago and the 71 average. The crop was rated two percent excellent, 28 good, 45 fair, 24 poor and one very poor.
Oats were 75 percent headed versus 80 a year ago and the 50 average. The crop was rated seven percent good, 70 fair, 22 poor and one fair.
Alfalfa was rated four percent excellent, 75 good, 20 fair and one poor. Pastures were rated six excellent, 58 good, 32 fair, three poor and one very poor.
